Description: Wild vervet monkey dyadic aggressive interactions, 66 animals, 2015-2017. One row per interaction with native draws and undecided outcomes.
Reference: Vilette, C., Bonnell, T., Henzi, P., & Barrett, L. (2020). Comparing dominance hierarchy methods using a data-splitting approach with real-world data. Behavioral Ecology, 31(6), 1379-1390.

Description: Comparative judgement of the relevance of mathematics text sections (parity and periodicity of real functions) to a question: 1,948 decisions by 78 undergraduate judges over 126 section codes, in six sessions with one question each (3 conceptual, 3 procedural). agent_a = section chosen as more relevant; rater = judge; session, question, question_type.
Reference: Makri, D., & Jones, I. (2026). Investigating Questions Driven Reading of Mathematics Data Sets. Loughborough University. Dataset.
Notes: Non-commercial (hostable, Ben 10-01). Section codes are per session, so the six sessions are disconnected. excluded = the platform's flag (all 25 decisions of judge JUDGE-C2-20), kept. Built by data/competitions/makri_2026_mathtext_relevance.R (#2688).

Description: Spotted hyena aggressive interactions, Happy Zebra clan, Masai Mara (Mara Hyena Project): 8,521 acts among 121 hyenas of all ages and both sexes. agent_a = aggressor = winner (acts the recipient ignored or counterattacked dropped, the talek_hyenas rule); context, intensity, recipient response and both parties' sex, status and age class kept.
Reference: McCormick, S. K., Laubach, Z. M., Strauss, E. D., Montgomery, T. M., & Holekamp, K. E. (2022). Evaluating drivers of female dominance in the spotted hyena. Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution, 10, 934659.
Notes: Talek clan excluded (already in talek_hyenas_*). No date in the source. The response-code mapping is in the script header; this is not the authors' stricter Win variable (submissive responses only). Some hyenas appear in more than one clan table. Built by data/competitions/mccormick_mara_hyenas.R (#2673).
